Work Order Description:
Issue Summary - VR Bench Systems

VR Bench 2 - Computer 1
Computer 1 on VR Bench 2 is intermittently powering off shortly after being turned on. The system does not consistently reach the BIOS screen before shutting down. During troubleshooting, it was observed that the VR headset still powers on; however, it does not initialize correctly for the VR games because the computer is not completing the boot process. The PC also did not power itself off during every startup attempt, indicating the issue is intermittent.

Additional Findings
A similar issue has been identified with a computer on VR Bench 1, which is exhibiting the same intermittent power behavior. In addition, all other seats on both VR benches power on except for one station that is failing to display any video output.

Current Status
Troubleshooting has confirmed multiple hardware-related symptoms across both VR benches. Further diagnostics are required to determine whether the root cause is related to the power supply, motherboard, memory, graphics hardware, display connections, or another underlying hardware component.

Work Order Title:
TSR-SLSC-027 
Port Door Limit Switch Damaged
Work Order Description:
During operation yesterday, 3/19, the Port Door Limit Switch was struck by the Roll Arrestor Bar. The operator did not notice that the machine had fallen badly out of calibration as the ride ended. The force of the bar knocked the switch clean off of its mount.

Upon investigation, I discovered that the provided bolts do not attach securely to the frame. The 026 port switch screws were different and larger, but did not fit the 027 switch mounting plate. As our 026 is currently inoperable, I simply switched the mounting plates and used the larger screws. 

This means, though, that the 026 port door limit switch is not secured, and the provided bolts (even others we have in storage) do not fit securely. Are there different sizes in the limit switch mounting plates? Our 026 machine switch was the only one that was different in our inventory.

Neville

Work Order Title: Max-Flight Simulators, AKA "GForce" Pre-Opening Maintenance and Repairs
Work Order Description:
Hey Team,

During Father's Day weekend, I was asked to do a soft opening of the Max Flight simulators, known as the "G-Force Encounter" and encountered numerous issues that needed to be addressed.

We had an on-board computer that would not power up; no LED to indicate that the motherboard is powering up; swapping the external power supply did not fix the problem.  I installed and programmed a spare on-board computer we had and that fixed the problem.  We will need to send the bad computer back to maxflight for repairs.

Two of the 4 training stations' computers are not firing up; they're dead.  To open on that weekend, I only operated two of the training stations.

The flight sticks on the trainers and simulators are Happ analog flight joysticks with 5k-ohm potentiometers.  Unfortunately, with the ship closed and humidity in the ship caused surface corrosion on many of the hardware; sadly the potentiometers were affected and they are not reading correctly, making the  flight control difficult.   I have the necessary number of potentiometers to replace them all, but with my short staffing issues, repairs have been delayed to only when I have the free time.

As for the trainers, I will need to replace these dead computers; I am able to get refurbished desktops locally and installed on the same day; the game itself is an old  "combat flight simulator 2" game  that I have on a flash drive and will install in any computer, training kiosk or on-board the simulator.

The simulators themselves have been in operation since they were replaced in 2008 and have undergone some updates and repairs to keep them operational.  

We keep a minimal number of parts to make some repairs, but for any larger repairs we count on MaxFlight to have the parts sent to us.   Some components that fail  that we get from Maxflight are seatbelts, canopy latches and lanyards and lift shocks.  Flight sticks, throttles and repair parts for them we buy from SuzoHapp, while hardware is purchased from either McMaster or locally.

Team, our two Max-Flight simulators and trainers use Flight Sticks, Throttles and USB controllers manufactured by SuzoHapp.  Generally, these components do have a tendency to wear out from heavy use.  The potentiometers on the flight sticks do wear out the fastest, but the USB boards have a tendency to go bad as well.

We generally want to keep a supply of often needed parts on hand to speed up repairs and prevent downtime.  Over the years, these components have increased in price and thus we try to only have the absolutely necessary items on hand.

With Fleet Week coming up in late May, I find it necessary to ensure we replenish our spare parts stock.

I have ONE USB controller on hand and TWO spare potentiometers; 8 pots were replaced when we reopened last year, so we are due to have pots begin to fail. 

I need to have at least 8-10 pots on hand (4 pots on each simulator X2, plus 2 pots on each trainer X4); while 8-10 are not enough to replace all of them, it provides a safe buffer to at least keep the simulators functional.

I also need at least 2 more USB Controllers (each simulator has 2 controllers X2, plus one in each trainer X4). Again, only enough to keep simulators running.

https://na.suzohapp.com/products/joysticks/50-2064-00 is the link for the 5K, S-Taper 3/4" potentiometers.  At $48 each, it's getting expensive to replace before each season, but rather when necessary.  Unfortunately, they appear to be on backorder at least until September, so if more than 2 fail before that time, we could face a substantial downtime.

https://na.suzohapp.com/products/joysticks/95-0800-20 is the USB Game Controller. At $275 each, they are not cheap to keep several in stock.  It apperas that the soonest they'll have availability is in two week's time.

I would like to know what type controllers are used with the joysticks in the I-360 and wonder if it could be adapted.

Another alternative I have seen are these; they are manufactured in England. 
http://www.leobodnar.com/shop/index.php?main_page=product_info&cPath=94&products_id=180

It could be possible to adapt these to our systems and eventually replace all of the HAPP Controllers at a fraction of their cost.  

I do hope HAPP understands our dire need to have these parts on hand before the beginning of our busiest week since the pandemic and are able to supply us with our request.

Work Order Title: TSR - intrepid - TFX Hydraulic System Accumulator in need of Nitrogen Servicing
Work Order Description:
The Transporter FX simulator (6-axis Galaxy) has an emergency recovery system that in the event of a power failure, the system sends a signal to all the moog valves to put themselves in the down position and the stored fluid under pressure in the accumulator will lower the entire capsule to its base.

The accumulator is basically a very thick bladder inside the cylinder and it is normally pressurized to about 1200-1300psi.  When hydraulic pressure is applied (between 1500 to 1800psi) the bladder will compress and the hydraulic fluid will fill the cylinder; this stored fluid under pressure is released during a power failure to lower the ride completely so emergency egress procedures can be performed.

During training and testing, the power was removed while the simulator was in use and there was insufficient fluid or pressure to lower the entire base; instead it squatted like a dog with the runs..., or a customized SC truck (had to make you visualize and give you a good laugh).  This position makes it impossible to lower the bridge and/or open the door.

The last time this cylinder was serviced was a decade ago.  It's necessary to get this system operational to ensure emergency egress can be done safely.

Work Order Title: Tsr-Intrepid-XD Theater seats 11 and 12 are not moving
Work Order Description:
The Trio-Tech XD Theater aboard Intrepid was originally installed on October 2008 with 14 seats.  In 2012, an update to accommodate ADA required the removal of one seat, so we have 13 seats available.

The seats are controlled by a motion control module, with seats tied in pairs for each module, for a total of 7 modules.  Each module communicates with a pair of seat control boxes (labeled A1 or B1 Control Box) and two motor/actuators on each seat.  If a chair malfunctions, it could be a number of issues; the computer will stop the motion in both A1 and B1 control boxes and will provide a diagnostic message on screen that helps determine which seat malfunctioned.  Once the seat is isolated, a number of issues can be the culprit of the cause, such a a broken or non-communicating motor, a jammed or binding actuator, a bad control box or a combination of components.

In the current failure, we know we have seat 11 (A1 Control Box) and Seat 12 (B1 Control Box) not moving.  I will be able to isolate the  bad seat from the control module and have 12 seats operational, but that requires a reprogramming of the Theater Program, something I will not permit staff to access, as it can affect the operation of the theater.

ATM, we are severely short staffed (with very limited number of staff qualified to operate the TFX) so I am currently operating the TFX and unable to troubleshoot or isolate the issue until the end of the day in order to make the necessary repairs. 

We are still operational with 11 seats still in operation.

During an early morning 90-day maintenance of the projector, I saw more moisture then ever leaking onto the projector.  

On several occasions, I have alerted maintenance and ops that the insulation on the pipe is insufficient and condensation is leaking onto the projector.  This has caused water stains on the casing and without further care to prevent the leaks on the projector, it will reach its internal components, like circuit boards, light engine and or power supplies.  

I am requesting we have a drip pan placed directly under the cooling pipes that will drain this water down to a condensate pump, already present in the projection booth.

Work Order Description:
I was out of the office from Saturday-Monday, this is the email I got from one of my shift leads about errors we experienced with Client 4. I also recognize that we had significant staffing issues Saturday morning that prevented us from turning VR on until 12:30 when our afternoon shift got in. This is the account of issues and problem solving done by SMM's Shift Lead Riley over the weekend: 

Saturday, August 24th: When I arrived onsite at 12:30pm on Saturday, it took about 30 minutes to get a VR call for a shift lead from Nathan, and when I responded he explained to me that Client 4 was blacked out. I initially thought it was the familiar issue of a client shutting itself off, but saw that Client 4's space on the top monitor at the operator's station was a completely black screen, with the same lack of visual inside the headset. There was no indication that the Client was on at all, except for lights on inside the computer tower behind the seat. I took over troubleshooting and first opened Client Tools to confirm that the server was recognizing Client 4, which was the case, and restarted the client. This had no effect, so I restarted all clients to hopefully trick the server into realizing that Client 4 should be operational. However, the outcome of this was Client Tools showing three Client 4's, but the visuals still did not come back. In an attempt to solve the new anomaly, Nathan went down to each of the three Client 4 selections and restarted each individually, which temporarily solved the number of Client 4's, and somehow resulted in the server figuring itself out and recognizing Client 4 again. VR was operational for the rest of the night.

Sunday, August 25th: When our scheduled VR operator, who again happened to be Nathan, arrived onsite on Sunday morning and attempted to turn on VR, there was again no Client 4 and I responded to the radio call. We attempted the same troubleshooting steps as the day before, but the only change was that we had two Client 4 options instead of three, and so at 9:45am we called for assistance from Exhibit Maintenance. They had also never seen this issue before, and Nathan and I explained the steps we had taken and the results of troubleshooting the day before. Nothing they attempted had any effect, and Steve took a look at Client 4's tower behind the seat and let us know it was indicating there was no signal being transmitted.  We decided to completely turn off the machine, then wait two minutes and turn it fully back on again. This worked to solve the issue, and we worked out an action plan to check on the machine's function every hour to keep the clients all active and operational for the rest of the day. Later in the day, Client 4 had a brief fit while S.E. was operating the ride and no visuals would appear in the headset. I responded to the call and restarted Client 4 and reloaded the ride, then made sure all headsets had visuals when I recalibrated them. Everything at that point was operational. Finally, at roughly 3pm, Client 4 went completely black on the screen and in the headset again while Nathan was operating. I responded to the call and did the typical restarts, but they had no effect and so we called for Exhibit Maintenance. When we opened Client Tools again, Client 4 had completely disappeared from the selection menu and we could not access or communicate with it. Steve checked the tower out and it was indicating the same lack of signals as that morning, and so the three of us discussed and decided to operate VR with three functioning seats for the remaining two hours of the day. Client 4 had been erased from the server in some way, and there was no capacity to do another complete shutdown to possibly restore it.

Systems experience issues such as enemy assets not spawning or significant frame rate degradation that renders the experience unusable.

VR Headset Speaker Failures
Headset speakers frequently fail due to fragile plastic components or experience intermittent or complete audio loss.

VR Headset Cable Failures
Cable failures have been an ongoing issue since the current headset model was introduced.
